title: Non-Invasive Mood Tagging via System Playlists
context: We needed a way to tag tracks with moods (Focus, Chill, Energy) without modifying audio file metadata, which is fragile and risky for library integrity.
decision: Moods are stored as Navidrome system playlists using the convention NG:Mood:{MoodName} (e.g. NG:Mood:Focus). Audio files are treated as read-only artifacts.
consequences: Moods persist across library rescans. No risk of corrupting file tags. Playlists are portable. Downside: mood data is lost if Navidrome DB is reset.

title: FastMCP as MCP Server Framework
context: We needed a Python framework to expose Navidrome tools via the Model Context Protocol. Options: raw MCP SDK, FastMCP.
decision: Use FastMCP for its decorator-based tool registration (@mcp.tool(), @mcp.resource()) and built-in stdio/SSE transport. Single-file server architecture.
consequences: Very low boilerplate. Easier to maintain. Constrained to FastMCP release cycle. ANSI escape sequences on stdio are a known issue (stripped by wrapper in Antigravity config).

title: Stdio Transport over SSE for Local Development
context: Two MCP transport options: stdio (client spawns server as subprocess) and SSE (HTTP-based, requires running web server).
decision: Default to stdio transport. The MCP client reads a JSON config and spawns the Python process locally. No open ports, no firewall config.
consequences: Zero network config. Secure by default. Server must live on the same machine as the client. For remote scenarios, use SSH tunnel to Navidrome (not to MCP server).

title: JSON Structured Logging Decorator for All Tools
context: We needed observability into tool calls (duration, inputs, errors) without cluttering tool logic. Needed to track LLM prompt quality vs result quality.
decision: Implement a JSON logging decorator applied to all @mcp.tool() functions. Logs to file (configurable via NAVIDROME_LOG_FILE env var) or stderr.
consequences: Enables analytical feedback loop. Log path must be absolute or the directory creation fails (fixed in v0.1.3). Logs excluded from git via .gitignore.

title: Playlist Idempotency: Overwrite by Name
context: Calling create_playlist with the same name repeatedly created duplicates (Playlist, Playlist (1), Playlist (2)...), cluttering the library.
decision: manage_playlist(operation='create') detects existing playlists by name and overwrites them instead of creating duplicates.
consequences: Clean library. Agents can safely call create repeatedly without accumulating duplicates. Risk: an agent could unintentionally overwrite a user's playlist if names collide. Mitigation: NG: prefix convention for agent-created playlists.

title: Tool Consolidation: Multi-Mode Pattern over Fragmented Tools
context: v0.1.1 had separate tools: get_library_pillars, analyze_library_composition, analyze_user_taste_profile. This created LLM decision overhead and duplicated boilerplate.
decision: Merge into analyze_library(mode='pillars'|'composition'|'taste_profile'). Same pattern applied to manage_playlist (create/append/get/delete operations). Single tool, mode parameter selects behavior.
consequences: Fewer tools = less LLM confusion. Docstrings carry the WHEN/WHY for each mode. Aligns with mcp_tool_design KI consolidation principles. This pattern is now the standard for all new tools.

title: docs/ as Living Documentation (Single Source of Truth)
context: Documentation lived in memory-bank/ without clear structure or agent discoverability. Agents started each session with incomplete context.
decision: Migrate to docs/ with subdirectories: overview/, architecture/, roadmap/, artifacts/. Symlink docs/ to Antigravity global knowledge base. All agent rules reference docs/ exclusively.
consequences: Agents can self-orient via symlink. docs/metadata.json acts as KI descriptor. timestamps.json excluded from git to prevent false-positive diffs. Documentation updates are mandatory in same PR as code.

title: pyproject.toml for Modern Python Packaging
context: Project used ad-hoc dependency management. Needed reproducible installs for contributors and CI.
decision: Adopt pyproject.toml (PEP 517/518). Virtual environment via .venv. Enforced .venv usage in all agent workflows.
consequences: pip install . works from project root. .venv excluded from git. Contributors get consistent environments. Aligns with modern Python tooling standards.

title: Curator Manifesto: Harvest → Filter → Execute Protocol
context: Agents were creating playlists with a simple search → create_playlist call (The Lazy DG anti-pattern). Results had poor diversity and no quality control.
decision: Formalize the three-stage Curator Protocol: (1) Harvest 3x-5x target tracks, (2) Filter via assess_playlist_quality, (3) Execute only after passing the quality gate. Exposed as curator://manifesto MCP resource and curator_mode prompt.
consequences: All agent sessions inject the manifesto at start. Quality gate (assess_playlist_quality) is MANDATORY before any playlist creation. Pattern encoded in llm_tool_usage.md and .agent/rules.

title: Advanced Filtering in get_smart_candidates: BPM, Genre, Mood
context: Agents could only filter by mode. No way to constrain by energy level, genre, or BPM for mood-specific playlists.
decision: Add include_genres, exclude_genres, min_bpm, max_bpm, max_tracks_per_artist, and mood parameters. mood parameter (relax/energy/focus) auto-maps to BPM ranges and genre exclusions.
consequences: Much more precise curation possible. BPM=0 tracks strictly excluded when min_bpm is set (Silent Mode bug fix in v0.1.7). Metadata enriched with bpm, userRating, comment, path.

title: Tiered Similarity Lookup for get_similar_artists
context: Many libraries lack Last.fm-style direct similarity data. A simple similarity lookup returned empty results too often.
decision: Implement tiered fallback: (1) Direct artist similarity, (2) Bio/info data, (3) Genre-based peer matching. Returns results from whichever tier yields data.
consequences: Hit rate significantly higher in diverse/indie libraries. Genre fallback may be less precise but avoids empty responses. Documented in navigravity_debugging KI.

title: Smart Scoring Formula for Track Ranking
context: get_smart_candidates returned tracks with no quality signal — random order meant low-quality tracks competed equally with starred favorites.
decision: Implement smart_score = 3 (neutral) + (stars * 1) + (5 if heart/starred else 0). Sort results by smart_score descending, then shuffle within top tier for variety.
consequences: Starred tracks surface reliably. Low-rated tracks (1-2 stars) are deprioritized. Bug: initial impl used wrong key (userRating vs rating) — fixed in same release. Top-tier shuffling prevents deterministic repetition.

title: Automatic Batching for Large Playlist Saves (Race Condition Fix)
context: Saving playlists with >20 tracks to Subsonic API resulted in partial saves (race condition). The API call succeeded but only a subset of tracks were persisted.
decision: manage_playlist auto-batches track additions: 10 tracks per API request, with verification after each batch. Returns granular JSON feedback (added, dropped, batches counts).
consequences: Large playlists (50-150 tracks) save reliably. Slower than a single call but robust. Batch size of 10 chosen conservatively based on observed Subsonic behavior.

title: Mandatory ID Verification to Prevent Ghost Track Failures
context: Agents occasionally passed stale or Markdown-embedded IDs (e.g. [track_id]) to playlist tools, causing silent failures or corrupt playlists.
decision: assess_playlist_quality applies regex ID sanitization (stripping quotes, backticks, Markdown link syntax) before any API call. manage_playlist verifies IDs exist before attempting to add them.
consequences: Ghost IDs yield warnings, not hard failures. Agents receive explicit feedback on dropped IDs. ID sanitization is transparent to callers.

title: Agent Governance: Senior Methodical Engineer Persona + TDD-First
context: Development was ad-hoc. Agents sometimes wrote code without plans, skipped tests, or made changes that diverged from documentation.
decision: Formalize the Senior Methodical Engineer persona in .agent/rules/01-identity.md. Mandate: (1) implementation_plan.md before any code, (2) failing test before implementation, (3) docs updated in same session as code.
consequences: Higher development quality. Slower initial velocity but fewer regressions. Codified in .agent/rules/05-planning-standard.md. Workspace-local mcp-development skill enforces MCP-specific standards.

title: Handshake-Discovery Sync Protocol for MCP Resources
context: As tools evolved, the navidrome://info resource and usage_guide prompt lagged behind actual capabilities. Agents operated on stale self-descriptions.
decision: Any change to the public tool surface MUST update three resources in the same session: navidrome://info (version+capabilities), usage_guide prompt (instruction manual), curator://manifesto (philosophy). Encoded in .agent/rules/02-handshake-discovery.md.
consequences: Discovery resources stay current. Adds overhead to every feature PR. Risk of forgetting is mitigated by the rule being always_on triggered.

title: Rediscover Mode: Album-Level Archeology over Random Songs
context: Original rediscover mode selected random songs not played in >1 year. Results felt incoherent — unrelated tracks with no album context.
decision: Shift to Album Archeology: rediscover samples random albums (not random songs) not played recently, then picks tracks from those albums. Adds coherence and album narrative to rediscovery.
consequences: More musically coherent results. Users rediscover complete album contexts rather than isolated tracks. Implemented as rediscover v2 in v0.1.7.

title: list_playlists Tool: Solving the Blind Agent Problem
context: Agents did not know which playlists existed. They either guessed names (causing fuzzy match failures) or hallucinated playlist IDs.
decision: Add list_playlists tool that returns all existing playlists with their IDs and metadata. Agents MUST call this before any manage_playlist(operation='get'|'append') to avoid blind lookups.
consequences: Eliminates Blind Agent failure mode. Documented in llm_tool_usage.md as The Inventory tool. Agents can now verify mood playlists exist before expanding them.

title: reference_track_ids: Seed-Based Discovery Expansion
context: Agents could not expand an existing playlist's vibe. They had to start from scratch or guess similar content. No way to say 'find more tracks like these'.
decision: Add reference_track_ids parameter to get_smart_candidates. Pass an array of existing track IDs as seeds; the engine finds tracks similar to those seeds. Enables Mood Architect pattern.
consequences: Existing playlists become discovery seeds. Most powerful expansion technique available. Enables incremental mood library growth via append operations.

title: Relaxed Search Matching: Auto-Split on Artist/Track Delimiter
context: search_music_enriched returned empty results when queries used 'Artist - Track' or 'Track by Artist' format. The full string matched nothing.
decision: Auto-detect and split queries on ' - ' and ' by ' delimiters. Retry with artist and track as separate search terms if the initial query returns zero results.
consequences: Hit rate significantly improved for common query formats. Transparent to callers. May produce wider result sets on retry — agent should filter by relevance.

title: Japanese Aesthetic Mood Taxonomy (Komorebi, Tsukiyomi, Shigure, Soyokaze)
context: Generic mood labels (Focus, Chill, Energy) lacked the cultural and aesthetic specificity needed for high-quality curated playlists. Needed a richer vocabulary.
decision: Define four Japanese aesthetic moods as canonical NG mood categories: Komorebi (morning light/instrumental), Tsukiyomi (nocturnal/dark ambient), Shigure (melancholic rain/jazz), Soyokaze (gentle/acoustic). Each has defined genres, artists, and instrumental rules. Max 4 tracks per artist per mood.
consequences: Richer, more culturally coherent playlists. Instrumental enforcement for Komorebi/Tsukiyomi/Shigure prevents vocal intrusion. Pattern documented in docs/artifacts/curation_moods.md. Originally implemented in Dynamic Newton project scripts.

title: Echoes Interleaving: 1:5 Seed-to-Support Ratio for Artist Journeys
context: Building a 60-track journey around a seed artist (e.g. Lucio Battisti) risked artist saturation and incoherence if tracks were randomly mixed.
decision: Implement 1:5 interleaving ratio: 1 seed track followed by 5 support tracks (3 thematic + 2 surprise/divergent). Saturation limit: max 2 tracks per supporting artist in the full 60-track list. Priority: starred=True, then sorted by play count descending.
consequences: Artist journeys feel intentional and varied. Surprise tracks (e.g. Nu Genea for Italo context) prevent monotony. Pattern generalizes beyond Battisti to any seed artist.

title: BrainOS Minimal Bootstrap for NaviGravity Workspace
context: No cross-session agent context existed. Each session started blind — no record of project state, active decisions, or critical gotchas.
decision: Perform BrainOS Minimal Bootstrap: create .brainos/context-map.md (project state, key files, decision highlights, cheat sheet) and .brainos/decisions.jsonl (this file). Add .agent/rules/00-contesto-progetto.md as Rule 00 with context-map.md as mandatory startup read.
consequences: Agents start sessions with full project context. GS#9 meta-audit check passes. .brainos/ tracked in git (user decision: keep tracked for NaviGravity). decisions.jsonl populated via reverse engineering of changelog and architecture docs.
